{"id": "ef805c95-e2bb-4ab1-8294-dcc8afbbacba", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_X2VipSBwqUxdarYbidpdrx", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"# Release Readiness Review\\\\n\\\\n## Querying Existing Reviews\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-1: List reviews\\\\n\\\\nUser asks to see release readiness reviews (e.g., \\\\\"Show me recent release reviews\\\\\", \\\\\"List my reviews\\\\\").\\\\n\\\\n1. Call `list_release_tasks` with `taskType: \\\\\"RELEASE_READINESS_REVIEW\\\\\"` and optional filters (status, time range)\\\\n2. Present results in a clear format with review ID, title, status, and timestamps\\\\n3. **Close** \\\\u2014 Share the list and offer to show details if needed\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-2: Get review details\\\\n\\\\nUser asks about a specific review (e.g., \\\\\"Tell me about review abc123\\\\\", \\\\\"What\\'s the status of my review?\\\\\").\\\\n\\\\n1. If user provides a review ID, call `get_release_task_details` with `recordTypes: [\\\\\"release_analysis_report\\\\\"]`\\\\n2. If ambiguous, call `list_release_tasks` with `taskType: \\\\\"RELEASE_READINESS_REVIEW\\\\\"` first to identify the target\\\\n3. Present the task status and report records\\\\n4. **Close** \\\\u2014 Share the findings\\\\n\\\\n## Starting a New Review\\\\n\\\\n**Automated testing resolution \\\\u2014 applies before EVERY new review (USE-CASE-3 and USE-CASE-4), no matter how the change was identified:**\\\\n\\\\nA release readiness review always runs static analysis on the change. It can *additionally* run automated testing: tests focused on the code changes under review are generated and executed in an isolated environment to surface runtime regressions that static analysis alone would miss. Automated testing makes the review more thorough but takes longer. If a user asks what automated testing involves, explain it in those terms.\\\\n\\\\nDetermine the testing preference **automatically from the association\\'s capabilities** \\\\u2014 do NOT ask the user:\\\\n\\\\n1. Call `list_associations` to retrieve the associations configured for this agent space.\\\\n2. Find the association matching the repository under review (match on `configuration.github.repoName` or `configuration.gitlab.projectPath`).\\\\n3. Check the association\\'s `capabilities` map for `RELEASE_READINESS_REVIEW_AUTOMATED_TESTING`:\\\\n   - If `capabilities.RELEASE_READINESS_REVIEW_AUTOMATED_TESTING.enabled` is `true` \\\\u2192 set `skip_automated_testing: false` (run automated tests).\\\\n   - If the capability is absent or `enabled` is `false` \\\\u2192 set `skip_automated_testing: true` (static analysis only).\\\\n4. If the `list_associations` call fails or the repository\\'s association cannot be found, fall back to omitting `skip_automated_testing` entirely (let the review agent decide).\\\\n\\\\n**Never ask the user** whether to run automated tests or static analysis only. The configuration in the admin console is the source of truth.\\\\n\\\\n**Automated testing must be enabled per repository before it can run.** You CANNOT enable or disable automated testing from chat \\\\u2014 users manage it per repository in their agent space settings. If a user asks to enable, disable, or otherwise change automated testing for a repository, tell them: \\\\\"Automated testing is enabled or disabled per repository in your agent space settings \\\\u2014 I can\\'t change it from chat, but once it\\'s enabled there I can run a review with tests.\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-3: GitHub Change(s)\\\\n\\\\nUser wants to review one or more GitHub changes (PRs, commits, or branches).\\\\n\\\\n**Complete information provided:**\\\\n1. Apply the **Automated testing resolution** above to determine the testing preference.\\\\n2. Call `github_get_release_readiness_review_input` with the repository and change details, applying the testing preference from the resolution.\\\\n3. Pass the result to `create_release_task` with `taskType: \\\\\"RELEASE_READINESS_REVIEW\\\\\"` and an appropriate title\\\\n4. Share the review ID and let the user know they can check back for results\\\\n\\\\n**Incomplete information:**\\\\n- **Missing repository**: \\\\\"Which GitHub repository is this for?\\\\\"\\\\n- **Missing change reference**: \\\\\"What\\'s the pull request number, commit SHA, or branch name?\\\\\"\\\\n- **Reuse context**: If the user mentioned a repo earlier, reuse it\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-4: GitLab Change(s)\\\\n\\\\nUser wants to review one or more GitLab changes (MRs, commits, or branches).\\\\n\\\\n**Complete information provided:**\\\\n1. Apply the **Automated testing resolution** above to determine the testing preference.\\\\n2. Call `gitlab_get_release_readiness_review_input` with the repository and change details, applying the testing preference from the resolution.\\\\n3. Pass the result to `create_release_task` with `taskType: \\\\\"RELEASE_READINESS_REVIEW\\\\\"` and an appropriate title\\\\n4. Share the review ID and let the user know they can check back for results\\\\n\\\\n**Incomplete information:**\\\\n- **Missing repository**: \\\\\"Which GitLab project is this for?\\\\\"\\\\n- **Missing change reference**: \\\\\"What\\'s the merge request ID, commit SHA, or branch name?\\\\\"\\\\n- **Reuse context**: If the user mentioned a project earlier, reuse it\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-5: Ambiguous Review Request\\\\n\\\\nUser asks to \\\\\"review my latest change\\\\\" or \\\\\"check my code\\\\\" without specifying provider or details.\\\\n\\\\n1. Ask which provider and what to review: \\\\\"Which GitHub or GitLab repository and change (PR, MR, commit, or branch) should this review be for?\\\\\"\\\\n2. Once provider is known, follow USE-CASE-3 or USE-CASE-4 reprompt pattern\\\\n3. **Never guess** repository names, PR/MR numbers, commit SHAs, or branch names\\\\n\\\\n## Checking Review Status\\\\n\\\\nWhen a user asks \\\\\"Is it done yet?\\\\\" or \\\\\"What\\'s the status?\\\\\":\\\\n\\\\n1. If review ID is known from context, call `get_release_task_details` with `recordTypes: [\\\\\"release_analysis_report\\\\\"]`\\\\n2. If ambiguous, call `list_release_tasks` with `taskType: \\\\\"RELEASE_READINESS_REVIEW\\\\\"` and `maxResults: 5` and ask which one\\\\n3. Report status (PENDING_START, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, FAILED)\\\\n4. If COMPLETED, share key findings from the report records\\\\n5. If IN_PROGRESS, let them know it\\'s still running\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Cancelling a Release Task\\\\n\\\\n### USE-CASE-6: Cancel a release task\\\\n\\\\nUser explicitly asks to cancel or stop a release readiness review (e.g., \\\\\"Cancel that review\\\\\", \\\\\"Stop review abc123\\\\\", \\\\\"Abort the release task\\\\\").\\\\n\\\\n1. If the user provides a task ID, call `cancel_release_task` with that ID\\\\n2. If ambiguous, call `list_release_tasks` to identify the target and confirm with the user before cancelling\\\\n3. Report the cancellation result (previous status and confirmed cancellation)\\\\n4. **Close** \\\\u2014 Confirm the task has been cancelled and no further action will be taken\\\\n\\\\n**Important:**\\\\n- Only cancel when the user explicitly asks \\\\u2014 never cancel proactively\\\\n- If the tool reports the task is already in a terminal state, inform the user it cannot be cancelled\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Shared Guidance\\\\n\\\\n## Capability Boundaries\\\\n\\\\n- You CAN trigger release readiness reviews to assess risk of code changes before deployment\\\\n- You CAN list and retrieve past review reports\\\\n- You CANNOT monitor progress in real-time \\\\u2014 users can check back or ask for status\\\\n- You CANNOT enable or disable automated testing for a repository \\\\u2014 that is managed in agent space settings\\\\n\\\\n## Task ID Format\\\\n\\\\nWhen displaying review IDs to the user, use this format for UI rendering:\\\\n\\\\n```\\\\n[[release-manager:<taskId>:<title>]]\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n**CRITICAL: Use the EXACT taskId from the API response.** Do NOT truncate or modify it. The title should be the task\\'s title from the API response.\\\\n\\\\n**Example:** API returns `\\\\\"taskId\\\\\": \\\\\"task-abc-123\\\\\", \\\\\"title\\\\\": \\\\\"Review PR #42\\\\\"` \\\\u2192 use `[[release-manager:task-abc-123:Review PR #42]]`\\\\n\\\\n**Important:**\\\\n- Do NOT include status, timestamps, or other metadata inside the `[[...]]` format\\\\n- Status can be shown separately after the format if needed, but not inside it\\\\n\\\\nUse this format in confirmation messages and when listing reviews.\\\\n\\\\n## Provider Vocabulary\\\\n\\\\nUse provider-native terms in responses:\\\\n\\\\n| GitHub | GitLab |\\\\n|--------|--------|\\\\n| workflow / workflow run | pipeline / pipeline run |\\\\n| workflow run ID | pipeline ID |\\\\n| job ID | job ID |\\\\n| failed step / failed job | failed job |\\\\n| pull request | merge request |\\\\n\\\\n## Terminology\\\\n\\\\n- Refer to these as \\\\\"release readiness reviews\\\\\" when talking to users\\\\n- The internal task ID should be called \\\\\"review ID\\\\\" when communicating with users\\\\n- Mirror the user\\'s vocabulary for pipeline concepts: if they say \\\\\"workflow\\\\\", respond with \\\\\"workflow\\\\\" (not \\\\\"pipeline\\\\\") unless clarifying\\\\n- Never expose internal terms like \\\\\"journal records\\\\\", \\\\\"agent input\\\\\", or \\\\\"task type\\\\\"\"}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}
